critique: The render reads as clean white snowfall on black, with appropriately varied speck sizes and a denser field by t4 that indicates ongoing emission. However, the snowfall is confined to a narrow central vertical column, leaving most of the frame empty; it feels like an emitter test rather than a full snowy-night scene. The flakes are also predominantly pinprick-small, so the result lacks the layered, softly visible snowfall presence expected from the preset thumbnail. Motion buildup from t1 to t4 is substantial, but the early frame is noticeably underpopulated.

suggestions.why: Widen the emitter so snow occupies nearly the full frame instead of a central column.
Increase vertical emission coverage so flakes enter across the visible image area rather than beginning in a compact band.
Make a portion of the flakes visibly larger and softer while retaining the existing 75% size randomness for depth.
